title: What If Mount Vesuvius Erupted Tomorrow?

scenes.text: What if Vesuvius erupted tomorrow? Hundreds of thousands of people live on its slopes.
Its alert level is green today. It last erupted in March 1944, and that eruption ran for about two weeks.
Planners prepare for a repeat of 1631, which killed roughly 3,000 people. Flows of hot gas and ash would race several kilometers downhill.
Those flows are the deadliest part, hot and fast. The red zone is drawn around them, and covers 25 towns.
Farther out, ash piles up. In 1944, 21 people died when roofs collapsed under it.
Scientists watch Vesuvius around the clock. Green today doesn't mean finished.

description:
What if Mount Vesuvius erupted tomorrow?
About 700,000 people live on its slopes, and its last eruption was in 1944.
Scientists monitor it 24 hours a day.
